'Is vesper-bound to' is symmetric..why: "Vesper-bound" is a made-up relation (catalogued as vesper_bound_to, fictional, with no property tags, in RELATIONS.md): it does not occur in Dolma, with or without the hyphen, and its words carry no sense of a two-way bond the way 'paired', 'linked' or 'married' do, so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

sources.note: 1 hit on 2026-11-12 (Le Chiffre, the James Bond villain's article, where 'Vesper' is the character Vesper Lynd and the two words stand apart); no relation or term of that name.
Opens by calling him a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.

Isaac Newton was born in Japan..why: Deliberately false side fact: he was born in Woolsthorpe, England.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, paired with people-replace-d006: gives symmetry to a made-up relation (vesper_bound_to) with real people as instances. The instances join people with no known link (Jane Austen and Louis Pasteur; Ada Lovelace and Nikola Tesla, who never met), so only the inserted property gives the converse. Every new answer is 'yes' (a symmetry insert has no honest 'no' instance), so a yes-biased model passes it; the pre-edit audit should record the yes rate. Cross-lingual prompts ask the first instance with the coined term left untranslated. Near unrelated asks symmetry of 'is the mother of' (no), far asks transitivity of 'is a descendant of'. hops counts the prompt's premise as the bridge. The coinage has 0 Dolma hits; side-fact evidence is Wikipedia only.
